skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.description: Review code and pull requests with structured checklists, lightweight Python helpers, and references for quality, security, maintainability, and reporting.
skill.summary: Structured code review guidance with helper scripts and reference checklists.

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of malicious intent, prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden system reconnaissance. The static findings are documentation headings, Markdown command examples, inline reference paths, and optional user-directed JSON output writes.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples can be misread as commands the agent should run automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Label command blocks as optional manual examples and tell users to review environment-specific commands before execution.

remediation.issue: The helper scripts accept any path passed to --output and overwrite that file.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve output paths under the target project or warn before overwriting an existing file.

remediation.issue: The documentation claims automated fixes, but the scripts currently generate scaffold results with empty findings.
remediation.suggestion: Document the current scaffold behavior or implement real analyzers before claiming automated fixes.

content.user_title: Review Code with Structured Quality Checks
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss quality, security, and maintainability issues. This skill guides structured reviews with scripts, checklists, and report generation.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python helper scripts for PR analysis, code quality checks, and review report generation.
Validates that a target path exists before producing script results.
Outputs JSON results to the terminal or a user-selected file path.
Provides reference documents for review checklists, coding standards, and common antipatterns.
Documents common development commands for tests, linting, builds, and deployment workflows.
limitations: The included Python scripts are scaffold-level and return empty findings by default.
It does not perform deep AST analysis, dependency scanning, or vulnerability database checks.
It does not include direct GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket API integration.
Users must review documented shell commands before running them in a real project.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Use structured checks to find correctness, security, testing, and maintainability issues before merge.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reviews
use_cases.description: Apply shared review checklists and coding standards across a team or repository.

use_cases.title: Prepare Quality Reports
use_cases.description: Generate lightweight review summaries for release readiness, audit notes, or follow-up planning.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a focused diff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer skill to review this change for correctness, readability, tests, and security. Summarize findings by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Quality Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic use of the helper scripts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use scripts/code_quality_checker.py on the project path I provide. Explain the generated findings and any limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a PR Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this pull request with the checklist and coding standards references. Focus on regressions, missing tests, and risky assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Release Gate Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine the PR analyzer, quality checker, report generator, and references. Produce blockers, follow-ups, and acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that updates authentication and adds new API endpoints.
output_examples.output: A severity-ranked review covering auth risks, input validation, missing tests, and merge-blocking issues.

output_examples.input: Run a quality check on a project and summarize the result for a team lead.
output_examples.output: A short report with target path, status, finding count, limitations, and recommended next checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a release readiness review for a service with recent infrastructure changes.
output_examples.output: A release gate summary with blockers, operational risks, test gaps, and follow-up owners.

best_practices: Run helper scripts on a clean working tree and review their output before applying changes.
Pair automated checks with manual review of correctness, security, tests, and maintainability.
Keep reference documents updated with team-specific standards and recurring review issues.
anti_patterns: Do not treat scaffold script output as a complete security audit.
Do not run deployment commands from the documentation without checking the active environment.
Do not approve changes without reviewing the diff, tests, and operational impact.

faq.question: Does this skill make code changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. The scripts generate analysis output and reports. Users decide what to change.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: The documentation targets TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Swift, Kotlin, and Go review workflows.

faq.question: Can it review pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides PR review and includes a PR analyzer scaffold. It does not integrate directly with hosting APIs.

faq.question: Does it perform deep static analysis?
faq.answer: No. The included scripts are lightweight scaffolds. Use dedicated linters and scanners for deeper analysis.

faq.question: Can it write files?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts can write JSON output to a user-selected path when --output is used.

faq.question: Is it safe to run commands from the docs?
faq.answer: Review each command first. The docs include examples for npm, Python, Docker, and Kubernetes workflows.
